svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.5.2 Lintels or Arches
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Lintels or Arches

g.text: Steel angle lintel over a veneer opening
TABLE 9.20.5.2. MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE SPANS FOR STEEL LINTELS SUPPORTING MASONRY VENEER
As printed in the 2024 source, both brick columns are headed "Supporting Brick" and some values carry a ">" mark the source does not
explain (not shown here). BCBC 2018 gives the same values under 75 mm brick, 90 mm brick and 100 mm stone.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Masonry over openings is supported by steel,
masonry or reinforced concrete lintels, or
masonry arches.
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry veneer
above openings
(a) conform to Table 9.20.5.2., and (b) have a
bearing length not less than 90 mm (3 9/16″).
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry other
than veneer, masonry and reinforced concrete
lintels, and masonry arches are designed to
Part 4 to support the imposed load.
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry are
prime painted or otherwise protected from
corrosion.
Drawn: only the front edge of the angle shows under the brick. Opening size is illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.5.2. (page 9-141)
